result.title: Probabilistic Monocular Biomechanical Reconstruction via Guided Flow Matching
result.summary: Reconstructing 3D joint kinematics from a single video is ill-posed due to depth and stature ambiguity, limb occlusion, and missing uncertainty estimates. We introduce the Biomechanical Flow Model (BFM), a continuous-time flow-matching prior over subject anthropometry, anatomical joint-angle trajectories, and virtual markers, trained on multi-camera clinical recordings from 565 participants and steered toward monocular 2D keypoints at test time without paired video training. In a head-to-head comparison on the same clinical trials against a state-of-the-art deterministic trajectory optimizer fitting the identical skeleton, BFM achieves comparable joint-angle accuracy across walking and timed-up-and-go (TUG). Across held-out control, prosthetic, and neurologic participants, BFM reaches 3.91 deg and 4.97 deg mean absolute joint-angle error on walking and TUG while providing credible intervals that bridge temporal and whole-limb occlusions. Where keypoints are hidden, the intervals widen with the error and keep their coverage near nominal. Supplying individual anthropometric calibration removes most monocular pelvis depth error, whereas testing on out-of-distribution pediatric crouch gait produces biased, overconfident extension predictions, highlighting the need for pathologically diverse movement priors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Biomechanical Flow Model，用 flow matching 学习人体测量、关节角轨迹与虚拟标记的连续时间先验，在多相机临床数据上训练，测试时仅用单目 2D 关键点引导采样，输出带可信区间的关节角估计。
AI.relevance_reason: 「测试时用稀疏视觉观测引导已训练好的生成先验、无需配对视频」以及遮挡处区间随误差加宽且覆盖率接近标称，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据如何注入 latent 状态、以及不确定性驱动的证据充分性判断提供可供核查的方法线索。
